newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain demands Rwanda explain aid worker murders.
newsitem.headline: Spain demands Rwanda explain aid worker murders.

text.p: Spain said on Monday it would ask the Rwandan government to explain exactly how three Spanish aid workers were murdered over the weekend and would demand that someone take responsibility.

"The Spanish government will demand that (Rwanda's) political leaders clarify the events and, where appropriate, demand someone claim responsibility," Fernando Villalonga, Spain's state secretary for international cooperation, told a news conference.
Rwandan Hutu militiamen shot dead three Spanish aid workers and three Rwandan soldiers and seriously wounded an American in an attack on Saturday night in the northwestern town of Ruhengeri.
Foreign Minister Abel Matutes told Spanish radio from Brussels that the European Union had decided not to send an international force to help stabilise the region.
"It's not because there isn't a serious situation...but a humanitarian force could present difficulties, and the remedy would be worse than the illness," he said.
"In fact such a force would be obliged to defend itself which would produce further violence and more deaths than if we did not deploy a force."
